主要内容: Apple's stock fell 7.1% over three sessions, wiping out $64 billion in shareholder value. The decline followed weaker-than-expected guidance from key suppliers, including Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, which forecasted second-quarter revenue of $7.8–7.9 billion versus Wall Street's $8.8 billion. TSM cited weak mobile demand as the cause. Austria-based AMS, a supplier of optical sensors for the iPhone X, also cut its second-quarter sales forecast to $220–250 million, down 50% from the first quarter. Analysts, including Bill Peterson and J.P. Morgan, noted the slowdown in Apple demand, particularly for the iPhone X, with Mizuho Securities predicting a 15% year-over-year decline in production for new models. Apple did not comment on the reports. The article highlights the impact of weak iPhone demand on Apple and its semiconductor supply chain.
